title: Microsoft 365 → Google Workspace Migration Program & Wave Plan (Enterprise/150k+)
author_notes: Effort tier: T5 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Move 150k users off Microsoft 365 without breaking the business
problem: Migrating 150k+ users from Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace is a program, not a project — and it fails without a disciplined wave plan, coexistence design, and cutover governance. This flagship solution provides the end-to-end migration program: discovery, wave planning, tooling strategy, coexistence, cutover runbooks, and hypercare across mail, Drive, and collaboration — executed pilot-first so waves run without architectural rework.
whats_inside: Program Overview — the migration operating model (discovery → design → coexistence → waves → cutover → hypercare) and how the workstreams sequence.
Wave Planning & Tooling Strategy — how to segment 150k users into waves, choose and govern migration tooling/patterns (mail, Drive, Chat), and define coexistence during the transition.
Cutover Runbooks — per-wave runbooks (readiness, mail-flow/DNS, data move, validation, rollback) and the go/no-go gates for each wave.
5 supporting scripts — source-estate discovery (M365/Entra), per-wave readiness validation, a migration-progress/coverage report, safe remediation, and a wave target-group builder.
Governance hooks + a Migration-Program playbook and Best Practices for executing waves without rework, plus Testing/validation gates.
short: The end-to-end M365 → Google Workspace migration program for 150k+ users — discovery, wave planning, tooling strategy, coexistence, cutover runbooks, and hypercare — executed pilot-first so waves run without rework. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
